title: Mazagon Dock, Mahanagar Gas Lead Nearly 100 Stocks Going Ex-Record This Week
excerpt: Defence shipbuilder Mazagon Dock's 92% final dividend and Mahanagar Gas's record-date action top a busy week of corporate actions on Indian exchanges.
body:
• Nearly 100 Indian stocks will turn ex-dividend or ex-record between August 17 and August 21, across dividends, bonus issues, and stock splits.
  • Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders goes ex-dividend on August 20 with a 92% final dividend for FY 2025–26, ahead of its August 27 AGM.
  • Mahanagar Gas turns ex-dividend on August 18, offering a trailing yield of 2.63% — one of the highest among upcoming payouts.
  • GE Vernova T&D India, LIC Housing Finance, and Zen Technologies are among other notable names with ex-dates on August 21.

Indian investors face a packed week of corporate actions as nearly 100 stocks turn ex-record between August 17 and August 21, with dividends, bonus issues, and stock splits all in play. Investors must hold shares before the ex-date to qualify for payouts — buying on or after the ex-date means missing the dividend.

Monday, August 18: Mahanagar Gas and More

Mahanagar Gas Limited (MGL), the Mumbai-based city gas distributor, goes ex-dividend on Monday with a final dividend payout. The stock carries a trailing dividend yield of 2.63%, making it one of the more attractive income plays in the week's roster, according to Stockopedia data. MGL shares have fallen roughly 12% over the past year, trading around ₹1,139.

Other stocks turning ex-record on Monday include Bombay Oxygen Investments (25% final dividend), Jay Bharat Maruti (35%), India Gelatine & Chemicals (60%), NGL Fine Chem (35%), and Rossell India (20%), according to exchange data compiled by IPO Watch.

Tuesday, August 19: Honda India Power, Foseco Crucible

Tuesday's ex-dividend list is headlined by Honda India Power Products with a 230% final dividend and Foseco Crucible (India) at 250%. L G Balakrishnan & Bros (220%) and Kovai Medical Center & Hospital (150%) round out the day's notable payouts.

Wednesday, August 20: Mazagon Dock's Big Payout

The week's marquee action comes on Wednesday when Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders goes ex-dividend for its 92% final dividend for FY 2025–26. The state-owned defence shipbuilder, which builds submarines and warships for the Indian Navy, has been a consistent dividend payer — it declared a ₹7.50 per share interim dividend in February 2026 and has paid dividends totalling ₹18.12 per share over the trailing twelve months, according to Stockopedia.

"Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders has informed the Exchange that the Record Date for the purpose of Final Dividend for the Financial Year 2025–26 is 20 August 2026."

— BSE Filing

The company's 93rd Annual General Meeting is scheduled for August 27. Mazagon Dock shares trade around ₹2,580, with a trailing dividend yield of 0.72% and a market capitalisation exceeding ₹1 lakh crore. The stock has underperformed the broader market over the past year, falling roughly 10%.

Also going ex-record on Wednesday are Marksans Pharma (90% final dividend), Kuantum Papers (250%), Sukhjit Starch & Chemicals (20%), Amarjothi Spinning Mills (22%), and Dai-ichi Karkaria (15%).

Thursday, August 21: GE Vernova, LIC Housing, Zen Tech

Thursday brings another cluster of significant payouts. GE Vernova T&D India leads with a 500% final dividend, followed by LIC Housing Finance (500%), KSE Ltd (750%), Hitachi Energy India (400%), A.K. Capital Services (220%), and Zen Technologies (100%).

LIC Housing Finance, the mortgage lender backed by Life Insurance Corporation, offers one of the week's largest absolute payouts at ₹50 per share. Zen Technologies, the defence electronics maker that has benefited from India's push for indigenous military hardware, rounds out its maiden year of high-profile dividends.

What NRI Investors Should Know

For NRI investors holding Indian equities through NRE or NRO demat accounts, dividends are subject to tax deducted at source (TDS) at 20% under Section 196D of the Income Tax Act, unless a lower rate applies under a Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA). Investors in the US, UK, and Canada can typically claim credit for Indian TDS against domestic tax liability.

The key deadline is simple: to receive any dividend, shares must be in the demat account before the ex-date. Given settlement cycles, the effective last buy date is typically one trading day before the ex-date.

Looking Ahead

The coming weeks remain busy for corporate actions. Procter & Gamble Hygiene and Health Care goes ex-dividend on August 25 with a 600% final dividend, while Gillette India follows on August 24, also at 600%. The AGM season continues through September, with several companies expected to announce interim dividends alongside their annual meetings.
